payload.title: A two-way table of class and music activity: probability and a chi-square test

stimulus.description: Two-way table of class and music activity for 240 students.

data.title: Class and music activity of 240 students

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: The two-way table shown comes from a random sample of $240$ students. One student is selected from the sample at random. Given that the selected student's class is freshman, what is the probability that the student is in the band? Round to three decimal places.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: The researcher plans a chi-square test of independence with these data. State the null and alternative hypotheses and the degrees of freedom.
parts.model_answer: $H_0$: class and music activity are independent in the population of students at a large high school; $H_a$: class and music activity are not independent (are associated). $df = (3 - 1)(3 - 1) = 4$.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Calculate the expected count for the cell of the students whose class is freshman and who are in the band, when the null hypothesis is true. Then verify that the large counts condition is met for the test.
parts.model_answer: Expected count $= (60)(85)/240 \approx 21.25$. All of the expected counts are at least $5$ (the smallest is $12.25$), so the large counts condition is met.

review.summary: The arithmetic checks out, but the stem never names the population. The model answers in parts B and E refer to "students at a large high school", which the student cannot see in the stem or the table. The rubric rows for the large counts check (C2) and the P-value (D2) are also loosely specified and need tolerance or required-element wording fixed.

scope_skill.notes: Parts match their own skills and the related topics 2.6, 3.14 and 3.15. Only part A covers topic 2.6.

key_scoring.notes: The key relies on a population ("a large high school") that the stem does not define. Row C2 does not require showing that the smallest expected count is at least 5. Row D2 requires 0.1493 with no stated tolerance, so a student answering 0.149 could lose the point.

stimulus_expression.notes: The table data are complete. The context lacks the population and sampling description needed for the hypotheses and the conclusion. The stem also does not ask for the random and independence conditions.

distractor_explanation.notes: This is a free-response item, so there are no MC distractors. The rubric common_errors entries are reasonable.
